documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Technology Usage Guidelines
documents.summary: An IT-office guideline for all students, employees and third parties using AI on university resources. It welcomes responsible use, recommends Copilot, and spends most of its text on data protection, verification of output, vendor risk review, security and monitoring. A single paragraph on academic integrity points to UAM 6,502 and says AI use should be disclosed as appropriate.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines "advocate for fostering curiosity and responsible usage of AI tools" and recommend Microsoft Copilot, so AI use is welcomed with conditions on data protection, verification and risk review. They defer to UAM 6,502 for academic integrity and say users should "disclose the use of AI in academic settings as appropriate" but set no course-level rule, so permit with conditions rather than delegates. Coder B coded delegates; re-reading the source, the page does not hand the decision to instructors (it names no instructor role), it welcomes AI use and attaches conditions on data protection, verification, risk review and disclosure, so permit.

documents.summary: Official UNR AI-site guidance for instructors on writing a syllabus statement. It recommends including a statement and discussing it on day one, then gives sample language for permitted, partly allowed and banned courses, tied to the academic integrity policy UAM 6,502. documents.summary: A teaching-center page that urges instructors to try AI tools, write a syllabus statement and discuss it with students. It argues for AI literacy and lists ways to use AI for course preparation and as a tutor or peer for students. It has few rules; its one firm line is that AI output is a draft to be reviewed.
documents.stance_why: The page leaves AI policy to instructors: it says views "fall loosely into 3 categories" and recommends only that each instructor write a syllabus statement. Most of the text suggests ways to teach with AI, and it sets no university rule, so delegates.
